units.human_topic: A Dedekind algebra is constructed on the generated subset, not necessarily the whole original set.
units.sense: Existence of a Dedekind-infinite set gives a singly generated Dedekind algebra whose carrier is a subset of it.
units.brief_arabic: الجبر يُنشأ على مجموعة جزئية مولَّدة؛ لا يلزم أن تكون حامله المجموعة الأصلية كلها.
units.rationale: The formal theorem asserts existence, and the proof takes A to be the closure of o under g inside D and restricts g to A. The old English/MSA lead-in instead suggests that every whole Dedekind-infinite carrier can be converted into such an algebra. Classical already expresses the existential consequence. The chosen MSA retains that reading and adds على مجموعة جزئية منها, identifying the carrier used by the proof. The theorem, both proofs, and the earlier C051-01 closure correction remain unchanged. This is a new source-based assessment, not a recovery of earlier translator intent.
units.counterexample: For D=Nat×{0,1}, g(n,b)=(n+1,b) and o=(0,0), the closure is Nat×{0}, a proper subset. More decisively, every singleton-generated successor algebra is the orbit {f^n(o):n in Nat} and hence at most countable. D=P(Nat) is Dedekind infinite via the injective map X↦{n+1:n∈X}, which omits {0}; Cantor diagonalization makes D uncountable, so no such algebra has all of D as carrier.

english.excerpt:
Since $A = \closureofunder{f}{o}$, our earlier result tells us that
$A$ is the smallest $f$-closed set with $o$ as !!a{element}. Clearly a
Dedekind algebra is Dedekind infinite; just look at clauses
\olref{ded:proper} and \olref{ded:injection} of the definition. But
the more exciting fact is that any Dedekind infinite set can be turned
into a Dedekind algebra. 

\begin{thm}\ollabel{thm:DedekindInfiniteAlgebra}
If there is a Dedekind infinite set, then there is a Dedekind algebra.
\end{thm}

\begin{proof}
Let $D$ be Dedekind infinite. So there is an injection $g \colon D \to
D$ and an element $o  \in D \setminus \ran{g}$. Now let $A =
\closureofunder{g}{o}$; by \olref{closureproperties}, $A$ exists and $o \in A$. Let $f =
\funrestrictionto{g}{A}$. We will show that $A, f, o$ comprise a Dedekind
algebra.

\begin{thm}\ollabel{thm:DedekindInfiniteAlgebra}
إذا وجدت مجموعة لانهائية بحسب ديديكند، وجد جبر ديديكند.
\end{thm}

\begin{proof}
لتكن $D$ لانهائية بحسب ديديكند. إذن توجد دالة متباينة $g \colon D \to
D$ وعنصر $o  \in D \setminus \ran{g}$. والآن لنجعل $A =
\closureofunder{g}{o}$؛ وبحسب \olref{closureproperties}، توجد $A$ ويكون
$o \in A$. ولنجعل $f =
\funrestrictionto{g}{A}$. وسنبين أن $A, f, o$ تشكل جبر ديديكند.

\begin{defn}\ollabel{Closure}
	لتكن $A$ مجموعة، ولتكن $f\colon A\to A$. تكون المجموعة
	$X\subseteq A$ \emph{منغلقة} تحت $f$
	{إذا وفقط إذا} كان $(\forall x \in X)f(x) \in X$. ولكل $o\in A$ نعرّف:
	$$\closureofunder{f}{o} = \bigcap\Setabs{X}{X\subseteq A\text{ و}o \in X\text{ و}X
	\text{ منغلقة تحت $f$}}$$
\end{defn}

\textbf{تنبيه تصحيحي على الأصل (C051-01).} قُيّد تعريف الإغلاق بدالة
$f\colon A\to A$، وجُعلت المجموعات المتقاطعة جزئيات من $A$؛ فعبارة
«لكل دالة» لا تكفل أن يبقى تطبيق $f$ داخل المجال ولا تعيّن المجموعة
المحيطة التي يؤخذ فيها التقاطع.

units.human_topic: The induction hypothesis uses the final index, not the number of sequence entries.
units.sense: The sequence A_0,...,A_n has final index n and length n+1; the displayed strong-induction parameter is n.
units.brief_arabic: الاستقراء على رقم الحد الأخير؛ المتتالية المرقمة من صفر إلى n طولها n+1.
units.rationale: The proof explicitly inducts on n for a sequence indexed from 0 through n. Calling the smaller parameter m a length mismatches that parameter by one. Classical already says رقم حدّها الأخير. Propagating this wording keeps every displayed bound and formula unchanged. The same repair is made separately at the later application to the two prefixes. The earlier general statement that actual sequence length can be used for induction is true and is preserved.
units.counterexample:
In the formation sequence , n=1. Its required prefix

has length 1, which is not less than n, but final index 0, which is less than n. Generally a prefix ending at j=n-1 has length n and final index n-1. The n=0 induction hypothesis is vacuous and the atomic case supplies the base.

alternatives.reason: A legitimate alternative induction measure only if all parameters and bounds are reindexed to actual lengths. That would needlessly change formulas here.
May express subscript more technically, but no exact official-dictionary attestation was checked; رقم follows the already coherent Classical reading.

units.uncertainty: High confidence in the off-by-one diagnosis. The preferred Arabic label for final index remains open to expert correction; no new induction principle or formula reindexing is claimed.

english.excerpt:
Suppose $!A$ has a formation sequence $\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_n}$.
We prove that $!A \in \Frm[L_0]$ by strong induction on~$n$.
Our induction hypothesis is that every string of symbols with a
formation sequence of length $m < n$ is in~$\Frm[L_0]$.
By the definition of a formation sequence, either $!A_n$ is
atomic or there must exist $j,k < n$ such that one of the
following is the case:
\begin{enumerate}
    \tagitem{prvNot}{$!A_n \ident \lnot !A_j$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvAnd}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \land !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvOr}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \lor !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvIf}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \lif !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvIff}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \liff !A_k)$.}{}%
\end{enumerate}
Now we reason by cases. If $!A_n$ is atomic then
$!A_n \in \Frm[L_0]$. Suppose instead that $!A \equiv
(!A_j \land !A_k)$. By \olref[pl][syn][fseq]{lem:fseq-init},
$\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_j}$ and $\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_k}$ are
formation sequences for $!A_j$ and~$!A_k$ respectively. Since
these are proper initial subsequences of the formation sequence
for~$!A$, they both have length less than~$n$. Therefore by
the induction hypothesis, $!A_j$ and~$!A_k$ are in~$\Frm[L_0]$,
and so by the definition of !!a{formula}, so is
$(!A_j \land !A_k)$. The other cases follow by parallel
reasoning.

msa.excerpt:
افترض أن لـ~$!A$ متتالية تكوين $\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_n}$.
نثبت أن $!A \in \Frm[L_0]$ بالاستقراء القوي على~$n$.
وفرض الاستقراء هو أن كل سلسلة رموز لها متتالية تكوين رقم حدّها الأخير
$m < n$ تنتمي إلى~$\Frm[L_0]$. وبحسب تعريف متتالية التكوين، إما أن
تكون $!A_n$ ذرية، وإما أن يوجد $j,k < n$ بحيث تتحقق إحدى الحالات
الآتية:
\begin{enumerate}
    \tagitem{prvNot}{$!A_n \ident \lnot !A_j$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvAnd}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \land !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvOr}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \lor !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvIf}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \lif !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvIff}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \liff !A_k)$.}{}%
\end{enumerate}
والآن نستدل بالحالات. فإذا كانت $!A_n$ ذرية، فإن
$!A_n \in \Frm[L_0]$. ولنفترض بدلًا من ذلك أن $!A \ident
(!A_j \land !A_k)$. بحسب \olref[pl][syn][fseq]{lem:fseq-init}، تكون
$\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_j}$ و~$\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_k}$ متتاليتي
تكوين لـ~$!A_j$ و~$!A_k$، على الترتيب. ولأنهما متتاليتان جزئيتان
ابتدائيتان حقيقيتان من متتالية التكوين الخاصة بـ~$!A$، فرقم الحد الأخير في كل منهما
أقل من~$n$. ومن ثم، بفرض الاستقراء، ينتمي كل من~$!A_j$ و~$!A_k$ إلى
$\Frm[L_0]$؛ ولذلك، بتعريف !!a{formula}، تكون
$(!A_j \land !A_k)$ كذلك. وتتبع الحالات الأخرى باستدلال مماثل.

supporting_primary_witnesses.excerpt:
\begin{defn}[Formation sequences for formulas]
\ollabel{defn:fseq-frm}
A finite sequence $\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_n}$ of strings of
symbols from the language~$\Lang L_0$ is a \emph{formation
sequence} for $!A$ if $!A \ident !A_n$ and for all $i \leq n$,
either $!A_i$ is an atomic formula or there exist $j,k < i$
such that one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
    \tagitem{prvNot}{$!A_i \ident \lnot !A_j$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvAnd}{$!A_i \ident (!A_j \land !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvOr}{$!A_i \ident (!A_j \lor !A_k)$.}{}%

english.excerpt:
Suppose $!A$ has a formation sequence $\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_n}$.
We prove that $!A \in \Frm[L_0]$ by strong induction on~$n$.
Our induction hypothesis is that every string of symbols with a
formation sequence of length $m < n$ is in~$\Frm[L_0]$.
By the definition of a formation sequence, either $!A_n$ is
atomic or there must exist $j,k < n$ such that one of the
following is the case:
\begin{enumerate}
    \tagitem{prvNot}{$!A_n \ident \lnot !A_j$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvAnd}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \land !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvOr}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \lor !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvIf}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \lif !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvIff}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \liff !A_k)$.}{}%
\end{enumerate}
Now we reason by cases. If $!A_n$ is atomic then
$!A_n \in \Frm[L_0]$. Suppose instead that $!A \equiv
(!A_j \land !A_k)$. By \olref[pl][syn][fseq]{lem:fseq-init},
$\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_j}$ and $\tuple{!A_0,\dotsc,!A_k}$ are
formation sequences for $!A_j$ and~$!A_k$ respectively. Since
these are proper initial subsequences of the formation sequence
for~$!A$, they both have length less than~$n$. Therefore by
the induction hypothesis, $!A_j$ and~$!A_k$ are in~$\Frm[L_0]$,
and so by the definition of !!a{formula}, so is
$(!A_j \land !A_k)$. The other cases follow by parallel
reasoning.

نثبت أن $!A \in \Frm[L_0]$ بالاستقراء القوي على~$n$.
وفرض الاستقراء هو أن كل سلسلة رموز لها متتالية تكوين رقم حدّها الأخير
$m < n$ تنتمي إلى~$\Frm[L_0]$. وبحسب تعريف متتالية التكوين، إما أن
تكون $!A_n$ ذرية، وإما أن يوجد $j,k < n$ بحيث تتحقق إحدى الحالات
الآتية:

    \tagitem{prvOr}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \lor !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvIf}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \lif !A_k)$.}{}%
    \tagitem{prvIff}{$!A_n \ident (!A_j \liff !A_k)$.}{}%

والآن نستدل بالحالات. فإذا كانت $!A_n$ ذرية، فإن
$!A_n \in \Frm[L_0]$. ولنفترض بدلًا من ذلك أن $!A \ident

\begin{enumerate}

units.human_topic: Every used premise must belong to the allowed set; not every allowed premise must be used.
units.sense: The used-assumption set is a finite subset of Γ, which itself may be finite or infinite.
units.brief_arabic: المقدمات المستعملة جزء من المقدمات المسموح بها؛ لا يلزم استعمالها كلها.
units.rationale: The earlier rule (2) admits any sentence belonging to the given Γ. The old parenthetical instead equates Γ with exactly the assumptions used. That excludes legitimate derivation witnesses with unused allowed premises and is incompatible with infinite Γ and finite derivations. Classical already requires each used premise to belong to Γ and visibly explains the source correction. Both its parenthetical and its note are copied exactly. The inference rules, axioms, theoremhood clause and worked derivation remain unchanged.
units.counterexample: For Γ={p_0,p_1,...}, the one-line derivation p_0 is justified by membership rule (2), but uses only {p_0}. No finite derivation can use every member of this infinite Γ. With Γ={p_0,p_1}, the same one-line witness still need not use p_1. This finite example distinguishes permissible witnesses, not whether another longer derivation could use every premise in a finite Γ.

supporting_primary_witnesses.excerpt:
Axiomatic !!{derivation}s are the oldest and simplest logical
!!{derivation} systems. Its !!{derivation}s are simply sequences of
!!{sentence}s.  A sequence of !!{sentence}s counts as a correct
!!{derivation} if every !!{sentence}~$!A$ in it satisfies one of the
following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $!A$ is an axiom, or
\item $!A$ is !!a{element} of a given set~$\Gamma$ of !!{sentence}s, or
\item $!A$ is justified by a rule of inference.
\end{enumerate}

وأبسطها. و!!{derivation}sها ليست سوى متتاليات من ال!!{sentence}s.
وتُعدّ متتالية من ال!!{sentence}s !!{derivation} صحيحًا إذا حققت كل
!!{sentence}~$!A$ فيها أحد الشروط الآتية:
